pages.text:
# Installing your App

* Copy for LLM

  Copy page as Markdown for LLMs
* View as Markdown

  Open this page as Markdown
* Open in ChatGPT

  Get insights from ChatGPT
* Open in Claude

  Get insights from Claude
* Connect to Cursor

  Install MCP server on Cursor
* Connect to VS Code

  Install MCP server on VS Code

Installation setup is dependent on whether your app is public or private.

## Private Apps: Install in your workspaces

You may want to install your app on a different development workspace for testing purposes or so you can use your app in the your paid production workspaces that you own.

Intercom workspaces for EU and AU

Development workspaces are for US region only. If you are using a development workspace to develop a private app, you will only be able to install your app into a paid Intercom workspace that is also in the US region.

If you are building a private app in EU or AU, we recommend using your paid Intercom workspace to develop the app; to use a development workspace, you will have to manually copy over your settings and endpoints into your paid workspace.

If you visit the **Test & Publish > Your Workspaces** page of your app in the Developer Hub then you should see all the workspaces you (as an Intercom teammate) are a member of.

You can click on **Install app** next to the workspace you want to install the given app on. This app will then be installed and an Access Token will be provided for that workspace so you can access its data through the API.

To rotate the access token for a Private app, open your app in the Developer Hub, click **Test and Publish**, then select the relevant workspace. From there you can click **Regenerate token** to issue a new Access Token or **Uninstall app** to revoke it entirely.

Consider how the app is being used before uninstalling

The app will no longer have access to data or be able to take actions on the workspace when uninstalled. Ensure uninstalling does not impact any workflows or teammates usage as it can be disruptive and is destructive. We give a warning box to ensure the action is deliberate before uninstallation and tell you where the app is currently being used if Canvas Kit capabilities are utilized.

## Public Apps: Set up your app for third-party installation

If your app is going to be public for any customer to install, you can set it as listed or unlisted.

For listed apps, customers may install your app directly from the Intercom App Store or through your product or website.

OAuth required for both installation types

Note that whether you decide to allow customers to install your app directly from the App Store or you provide installation through your own product or website, **OAuth must be configured** and functioning properly.

Unlisted apps do not need an Installation status

Unlisted apps do not need to fill out the Installation status section. Please provide clear instructions in your own product on how customers can install and use your app.

### Installation Status: Set the Installation URL

Third-parties (i.e. other Intercom workspaces) must authenticate via OAuth. This flow will be kicked off via a URL **hosted by you**, which should then redirect to the Intercom OAuth URL. Our Setting up OAuth tutorial provides details on how to set up the flow.

Once this flow is working, you need to decide where you want your app to be installed from. You can choose your method by going to the Installation status page of your Developer Hub under the Test and publish section.

When you click installation, you have the option to set a Direct installation URL (listed apps) or a Learn more URL (unlisted apps).

Canvas Kit requirements

If your app uses any form of Canvas Kit capability, **it's mandatory to allow your app to be installed through the listing on the App Store.** This is because apps which use the Canvas Kit work from within Intercom by default, are often discovered through the product itself, and have onboarding built in to the listing to help people get started.

This method allows customers to install your app directly from the listing in the Intercom App Store. This is strongly recommended because it drives higher install rates and reduces confusion on the part of teammates installing the app.

To choose this method, you will need to select **Directly from the Intercom App Store** from the form, and insert the URL that kicks off the OAuth flow in the **Direct installation URL** field.

Successful Installation

If installation was successful, you should redirect the user to `<https://app.intercom.com/appstore/redirect?install_success=true`>. This URL will bring them back to the App Store and will display a success message.

Failed Installation

If installation was unsuccessful, you should redirect the user to `<https://app.intercom.com/appstore/redirect?install_success=false&error_message=><your error message>`. You can fill in the `error_message` parameter with any error information you feel is beneficial for the end user to know.

### Allow installation from your own product or website only

Your app can also be installed through your own product or website exclusively. This means that you kick off the OAuth installation flow through your own product and redirect the user back there once complete.

For this method, choose **Through your own product or website** from the form. In the text field you must provide a **Learn more URL**. This URL must go to a page where customers can install your app. It's recommended to provide detailed steps on how they can install your app if it's isn't clear how to do so from the user experience.

You can use UTM tags if you want to track referrals from your listing.

### Uninstallation

#### Notifications

If you want to be notified when someone uninstalls your app or revokes access through any means, then you can optionally provide a URL for us to send you a POST request to.

You can use this to handle any cleanup or de-authorization on your side. The JSON payload will be as follows:

```
{
  "app_id": "abc123"
}
```

#### Revoking access

You can also uninstall an app and revoke access either for yourself or on behalf of a customer by making a POST request to the `https://api.intercom.io/auth/uninstall` endpoint with the given Access Token you want to deauthorize.

```
$ curl https://api.intercom.io/auth/uninstall \
-X POST \
-H 'Authorization:Bearer <Access token>' \
-H 'Accept:application/json'
-H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d
```

pages.title: Intercom developer FAQs | Intercom Help
pages.text: Use this article to set up your Intercom developer environment, configure a custom Help Center domain with SSL, authenticate your app via access tokens or OAuth, and manage contacts, conversations, and tickets via the Intercom API (Application Programming Interface). It also covers webhooks, pagination, building Messenger and Inbox apps, and troubleshooting common API and SSL errors. Intended for developers building integrations with Intercom. --- # Setting up Intercom ## How do I create a developer account? You can create a new developer workspace for developing apps. Developer workspaces are free and intended for development purposes only. Once you've created the new workspace you can follow this guide to create an app and make your first API call. You can create a new app for your production workspace and get the access token for the app by going to https://app.intercom.com/a/apps/{your-workspace-id}/developer-hub/ ## How do I set up a custom help center domain? When you turn on your Articles Help Center, your content is available through intercom.help by default. Your URL will look like this: intercom.help/exampleapp. If you'd like to use a different URL, you can create one by manually setting up a custom domain. This will involve entering the custom domain in your Help Center settings, creating a custom CNAME record, and optionally configuring SSL. Find the full instructions for set up in our developer documentation. If your Help Center shows a "not found" error after setting up a custom domain, verify your CNAME record to ensure your subdomain points to the correct Intercom host: • For HTTPS Quick Setup: us.intercomhelpcenter.com (US region) • For Manual/HTTP Setup: custom.intercom.help (US region) Also check that the security protocol selected in your Help Center settings matches your DNS setup. ### How do I set up SSL? SSL (or TLS), is the most widely used way to secure the connection between your server and your browser. It ensures the connection between the server and browser is encrypted and safe, and appears as HTTPS. There are two ways to set up SSL with Articles on your custom domain: * Use a flexible SSL (using a third party DNS provider like CloudFlare or AWS CloudFront) * Use your own SSL certificate (using a TLS Termination Proxy) ### ### Does Intercom handle SSL certificates for custom domains? Yes! If you enable “HTTPS (quick setup)” in your Help Center settings, Intercom will automatically provision and manage an SSL certificate for your custom domain (like https://help.ourdomain.com). There's no need for a manual SSL setup — just point your CNAME to us.intercomhelpcenter.com, and we’ll handle the rest. **Note**: HTTPS (quick setup) isn't available by default for all workspaces - it's a setting our Support team can enable for you. Once enabled, the HTTPS (quick setup) option will appear in your Help Center settings. Follow the DNS setup instructions below to complete your configuration. ### How to enable HTTPS (quick setup) for your custom domain If you aim to switch your custom domain to HTTPS: 1. Navigate to **Settings > Help Center > Configure & Style**. 2. Head to the **Domain** section. 3. Select **HTTPS (quick setup)** as your security protocol and save the changes. 4. Upon activation, ensure your CNAME record points to `[us.intercomhelpcenter.com](https://us.intercomhelpcenter.com)` (or `[eu.intercomhelpcenter.com](https://eu.intercomhelpcenter.com)` for EU regions) via your domain provider. You should receive a confirmation email when the setup is successful, typically within 48 hours. You can configure SSL for your custom domain to keep sensitive information encrypted. If you want to do this, make sure you’ve set up your CNAME with a DNS provider that supports SSL, like Cloudflare. Follow the guide in our developer documentation for setting up SSL. Note that depending on the provider you have chosen set up steps may vary. ### Advanced troubleshooting If the standard SSL and HTTPS configuration steps haven't resolved your issue, the following scenarios cover common edge cases for custom Help Center domains: * **HTTPS Defaults to Manual Setup:** Refer to our Custom Domains Guide for accurate configuration steps. * **Domain Displays as "Not Secure":** To secure your help center hosted on HTTP, consider: + Using a third-party DNS provider, such as Cloudflare or AWS CloudFront, for flexible SSL proxying. + Employing a TLS Termination Proxy for advanced SSL certificate management. ### Common HTTPS/SSL issues and troubleshooting **1. Domain Not Secure** * Ensure only Intercom's SSL certificate is active for your domain. Remove or disable any additional certificates from your host or CDN (Content Delivery Network). * If using a CDN such as Cloudflare, set the proxy status to "DNS only" (grey cloud icon). * Verify your DNS CNAME record points to the correct Intercom endpoint (us.intercomhelpcenter.com for US, eu.intercomhelpcenter.com for EU). **ERR\_SSL\_VERSION\_OR\_CIPHER\_MISMATCH Error** * Verify that your CNAME (Canonical Name) record points to `[us.intercomhelpcenter.com](https://us.intercomhelpcenter.com)`. * Confirm that no conflicting DNS (Domain Name System) records exist. Only one CNAME should be active for the domain entry. Delete any duplicates. * Ensure DNS propagation, which can take up to 72 hours, has been completed. You can use tools like whatsmydns.net to check global propagation. **2. HTTPS Setup Stuck on Pending** * Check for common DNS configuration issues, such as formatting errors in the CNAME record (for example, accidentally appending `.yourdomain.com`) or using an incorrect record type (for example, an A record instead of CNAME). * Ensure the CNAME record points to `us.intercomhelpcenter.com` (or `eu.intercomhelpcenter.com` for EU regions). * After corrections, wait for DNS propagation, which can take up to 72 hours. Use whatsmydns.net to verify global propagation before testing again. **3. HTTPS (Quick Setup) Option Not Available** * Contact Fin Support to have HTTPS quick setup enabled for your workspace — it isn't available by default. * Ensure your domain is not already in use by another Intercom account. * Verify that a CNAME record has been added to your DNS provider, pointing to `us.intercomhelpcenter.com`. **4. Access Denied Error** * Verify the CNAME record points correctly to `us.intercomhelpcenter.com`. * If using Cloudflare, set SSL to 'Flexible' or 'Full' — avoid 'Full (Strict)'. * Toggle the SSL configuration off and back on to restart the SSL provisioning sequence. --- # Help Center URL and domain management ## Broken URLs after migration If a migrated article URL no longer works after moving content to Intercom: * Create a new public article to replace the broken URL. * Update any calls to action or links in your content to point to the new article's URL. ## "Not found" error when articles look fine internally If your Help Center shows a "Not found" error on the public URL but articles appear correctly in your workspace: * Check whether your Help Center is set to Live in your settings. * Navigate to Settings > Help Center and set the status to Live to make the public URL accessible. --- # The Intercom API ## What is the current version of the API? The current version of the API is 2.18. You can find the documentation for the API on our developer documentation site. You can also change the version that your app is using in your Developer Hub by following the steps listed in this guide. If you are using the Intercom API, you can also change the version within the HTTP header of your request. **Note:** The developer documentation also keeps reference pages for the legacy 1.x API (URLs containing `/docs/references/1.0/` or `/docs/references/1.1/`). Those pages describe endpoints such as `/users` and `/leads` that aren't used in version 2.x. Make sure you're following the current version's reference pages under `/docs/references/rest-api/`. ## What endpoints are available in the current version of the API? Key endpoints available in version 2.18 of the Intercom API include the ones below. Newer APIs, such as Folders, Dynamic Content, Roles, Auth Tokens, and Granted Companies, are also available in 2.18. For the full list, see the API reference. ## Can I trigger an article to open in the Messenger from a button? Yes, if you'd like to trigger an article in the Messenger, you can use the `showArticle` method from the JavaScript API. The article will open within the Messenger and clicking the Messenger back button will return to the previous context. If the Messenger is closed when the method is called, it will be opened first and then the article will be shown. This is available across all platforms in the Messenger. ### How to trigger an article from HTML ``` # You can add a link anywhere on your site to open an article in the Messenger: Open article ``
